newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close sharply higher in correction.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close sharply higher in correction.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed firmer and just under the day's highs on speculative and local buying, which lifted the market out of recent lows made Thursday.
November FCOJ settled 2.75 firmer at 105.85, having ranged from 107.00 to 103.10. Spot September ended 2.75 higher at 115.75, while the back months finished 1.10 to 2.35 higher.

Market sources called today's move a correction to a slightly oversold market, adding that prices may have more room on the downside based on a weak technical picture. Dealers pegged support between 100.00 and 103.00 in November.
"We're in new low ground and have broken down completely," said Kevin Marshburn, an analyst with Fimat Futures.
He said prices would eventually climb to 112-115 basis November, citing bullish fundamentals such as strong weekly movement averaging about 5.0 million gallons, and dwindling supplies.

Expectations for the U.S. Department of Agriculture's next estimate of the Florida crop remain around 215 million 90-lb boxes. "Should the crop be smaller, futures are likely to advance back up to the 130.00 level fairly quickly," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
A higher estimate could pressure prices initially, but stronger production would be offset by lower imports into the U.S., preventing Florida stocks from accumulating, Ganes said.
The USDA will release the report in six weeks.
